title: Design the main screens
objective:
Design the complete app like a senior product designer: it is already written and working (step "Write the complete app"): the app frame, one shared store in src/app/, and working pages on the library's patterns: Saved [saved] in src/screens/SavedScreen.tsx, Product [entry] in src/screens/ProductScreen.tsx, Lists [lists] in src/screens/ListsScreen.tsx, List [mylist] in src/screens/ListScreen.tsx, Categories [categories] in src/screens/CategoriesScreen.tsx, Catalog [catalog] in src/screens/CatalogScreen.tsx, Find Stores [places] in src/screens/PlacesScreen.tsx. Search and suggestions, categories and filters, where each entry is found near the person's ZIP code, likes, saves, sharing, ratings and comments, and lists tied to a place already work across pages. Start your reply with the concept in 5 lines (idea, composition, type, colour, signature moment) and build to it.
- Keep those pages and the frame: never rebuild, replace or wrap them in new markup, and never give a page its own copy of the data. Give them this product's look through the Styles page (src/styles/tokens.css) and the pieces' fl-* classes in src/styles/components.css, and their words through their props (title, description and the like).
- Compose each of these pages as a finished page in its screen file, on the same data (lookup from src/app/lookup with useLookup from src/sections/LookupData for ZIP code, places, likes, saves, ratings and lists: const state = useLookup(lookup) gives the state (zip, placeId, signedIn, liked, saved, ratings, lists) and the actions are the lookup's own methods (lookup.setZip(zip), lookup.choosePlace(id), lookup.toggleSave(id), lookup.addToList(listId, entryId)), never destructured from useLookup; the parts take just lookup, e.g. <ZipPrompt lookup={lookup} />; store from src/app/store and useRecords from src/sections/AppData for the entries; the look-up pieces as parts, imported exactly so: import { CatalogSearch, CategoryIndex, LookupCatalog } from '../sections/LookupCatalog'; import { ZipPrompt, PlaceBadge, PlaceFinder } from '../sections/PlaceFinder'; import { LookupEntry, RatingsPanel, WhereToFind } from '../sections/LookupEntry'; import { ListIndex, ListBuilder } from '../sections/ListBuilder' (no other files hold them); go() from src/app/routes to open an entry): Home (src/screens/LandingScreen.tsx) [the landing page: FlowCode wrote a working start with the search, the ZIP code, the categories and the most liked; make it the product's own front page, with the PRD's promise and sections, keeping those working parts].
Run the app and look at each page at desktop and phone width before you finish.
The app: Clean Cart. Roles: Member (signed in as a demo account), Visitor (not signed in). Its data, store and navigation are written by FlowCode in src/app/ (schema.ts, store.ts) and src/App.tsx: every page reads and writes the same records through the store (src/app/store.ts), never its own copy.
- Products (product): Name*, Brand*, Category*, Certification*, Ingredients*, Short Description; statuses ; 20 sample records.
- Stores (store): Name*, ZIP Code*; statuses ; 8 sample records.
Navigation: Home (Home [landing], Search [not in this prototype], Saved [saved], Product [entry], Lists [lists], List [mylist]); Browse (Categories [categories], Catalog [catalog], Find Stores [places]).
A look-up app: people find product by category and search, and see which places near their ZIP code carries them (94110 Financial District, 94112 Mission District, 94114 Inner Richmond, 94115 Outer Mission, 94116 Haight-Ashbury, 94117 Tenderloin). Likes, saves, ratings, comments and lists live in the look-up layer (src/app/lookup.ts, from src/sections/LookupData) beside the store.

The screens already render the library pieces matched to them (Home → LookupCatalog.tsx; Home → LookupEntry.tsx). They are each screen's starting structure: keep them, replace every value in their SAMPLE object with the spec's real content (then delete the SAMPLE comment), and reshape them for this screen. If a piece really doesn't fit its screen, remove it and name it with the reason in your task_complete summary (for example "Removed FormFilters: the spec has no filters").

User journeys this prototype must support end to end (the screens link so each can be completed, with the same sample data throughout):

## Search for Product (Shopper; starts on Home; R13, R14, R15)
1. Home: Enter a search term in the search box → Navigate to Search screen with results
Success: Search results are displayed or no-results message if none match
If it goes wrong: No search term entered → Enter a search term and submit again

## Save Product (Shopper; starts on Product; R5, R17)
1. Product: Tap the Save button → If signed in, product is added to Saved; if not signed in, prompt to sign in
Success: Product saved or sign-in required
If it goes wrong: Not signed in when trying to save → Sign in (one tap in prototype) and then save again

## View Saved Products (Shopper; starts on Home; R18, R19)
1. Home: Navigate to Saved screen → Display list of saved products by name and brand
Success: Saved products are listed with links to their product pages
If it goes wrong: No saved products → Save a product first

## Open Saved Product (Shopper; starts on Saved; R18)
1. Saved: Tap on a saved product → Navigate to Product screen for that product
Success: Product page opens showing full details
If it goes wrong: No saved products → Save a product first

Screen briefs (locked: build every section with its part; if one truly doesn't fit, record the change with propose_layout_change and its reason, never leave it out quietly): design each screen to its brief, from the person's side. The top of the screen shows what they must see first (not a generic title over a list); the sections come in this order, each built from its catalog part (add_library_piece with the ID when it isn't in the app yet), filled with the spec's real content.

## Home
Page type: Marketing page (inform and persuade someone who isn't using the product yet). Not on this page: app data tables or admin controls.
For: Shopper. Goal: Find a product by name or brand in a few seconds; see featured products.
Workflow: 1. Enter a search term in the search box 2. Navigate to Search screen with results 3. View featured products 4. Tap on a saved product to go to Saved page
First view (without scrolling): What Clean Cart is in one line, a search box, and a few featured products.
Main action: Search for a product by name or brand
Sections, top to bottom:
1. What Clean Cart is: Introduce the app's purpose to the shopper.
2. Search Box: Allow the shopper to search for products by name or brand. [p.lookup-catalog]
3. Featured Products: Show a few popular or recommended products to the shopper. [p.lookup-catalog.grid]
States: loading: Loading featured products; empty: No featured products available; error: Failed to load featured products; success: Featured products displayed
On a phone: On phone, the search box and featured product grid stack vertically; top bar remains fixed.; one column; the main call to action near the top
Accessibility: Search box is keyboard accessible with label 'Search for products'. Featured product cards are labeled with name and brand.
Must satisfy: R13, R14, R15
